module.purpose: Provides an in-memory implementation of the synchronization storage contract, including document and object partitions, schemas, clocks, tombstones, snapshots, transactions, change feeds, and change notifications.
module.summary: This module implements synchronous transactional storage for synchronized records. It initializes room state from snapshots, separates object-lane records from document records, tracks shared document clocks and tombstone history, supports snapshots and incremental diffs, freezes stored records, and notifies subscribers after committed changes. Tombstone pruning is throttled to avoid blocking request handling, while transaction iterators reject consumption after closure.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative document synchronization and room state management. Failures can lose records, tombstone history, schema state, or incremental changes required by connected clients.

detail.name: computeTombstonePruning
preconditions: tombstones contains tombstone records with string ids and numeric clocks.
tombstones are ordered from oldest to newest for the returned pruning plan to represent the oldest entries.
documentClock is the current document clock used when no tombstones remain after pruning.
postconditions: Returns null when tombstones.length is less than or equal to maxTombstones.
When pruning is required, the returned plan identifies the first cutoff entries as tombstones to delete.
When pruning is required, the returned history-start clock is the clock of the oldest remaining tombstone, or documentClock when all tombstones are deleted.
The cutoff is advanced as needed so tombstones sharing the boundary clock are not partially deleted.
invariants: Tombstones at the same clock value as the deletion boundary are retained together rather than split.
Only a prefix of the tombstones array is selected for deletion.
edgeCases: When tombstones is empty or its length equals maxTombstones, returns null.
When tombstones.length exceeds maxTombstones, computes a pruning cutoff including the configured prune buffer.
When the cutoff reaches the end of the array, uses documentClock as the new tombstone history start.
When multiple tombstones share the clock at the initial cutoff boundary, advances the cutoff until that clock group is no longer split.
detail.summary: Determines whether tombstones exceed the configured limit and, when they do, returns a pruning plan that removes the oldest eligible tombstones without splitting a clock group. Returns null when pruning is unnecessary.

specTests.then: The result is null and no pruning plan is produced.
The deletion cutoff advances past the complete shared-clock group, so that group is not partially deleted.
The returned new tombstone history start clock is documentClock.

detail.signature: transaction<T>(callback: TLSyncStorageTransactionCallback<R, T>, opts?: TLSyncStorageTransactionOptions): TLSyncStorageTransactionResult<T, R>
preconditions: The transaction callback is expected to complete synchronously.
postconditions: The transaction is closed after callback execution, whether the callback succeeds or throws.
On normal completion, the callback result is returned through TLSyncStorageTransactionResult.
When opts.emitChanges is exactly 'always', changes are collected from the transaction relative to the document clock captured before callback execution.
invariants: The document clock used as the change-tracking baseline is captured before the callback runs.
The transaction is closed exactly through the finally path after callback execution.
Callback-thrown errors are not converted into successful results.
edgeCases: When opts is omitted or emitChanges is not 'always', change tracking is not requested.
When emitChanges is 'always' but the transaction has no changes since the starting clock, the changes value is absent.
When the callback throws, the error is logged and rethrown, and the transaction is still closed.
If the callback returns a promise-like value, the method remains synchronous and does not await it.

raises: The original error thrown by the transaction callback is rethrown unchanged.

stateMutations: Storage state may be mutated by operations performed through the transaction callback.
The transaction object's closed state is updated during cleanup.
detail.summary: Executes a storage callback within a transaction and returns its result, optionally including the changes produced since the transaction began. Callback failures are logged, propagated, and still cause the transaction to be closed.

specTests.then: The returned transaction result contains the callback's value and the forward diff generated since the document clock captured before the callback.
The same error is rethrown after being logged, and transaction cleanup still closes the transaction.

units.name: pruneTombstones

detail.name: pruneTombstones
postconditions: If the tombstone collection exceeds MAX_TOMBSTONES, the oldest tombstones are removed so the collection is bounded by the configured maximum.
If the tombstone collection does not exceed MAX_TOMBSTONES, tombstone contents are unchanged.
invariants: Tombstones are selected for removal in ascending clock order, oldest first.
The operation does not add tombstones.
edgeCases: When the tombstone collection size is at or below MAX_TOMBSTONES, no pruning occurs.
When the tombstone collection exceeds MAX_TOMBSTONES, entries with the lowest clocks are pruned first.
Repeated calls are throttled according to the throttle wrapper rather than necessarily executing immediately on every invocation.
stateMutations: The in-memory tombstones collection is mutated by removing selected oldest entries.
detail.summary: Throttled maintenance operation that bounds the in-memory tombstone collection by removing the oldest tombstones when the configured maximum is exceeded.

detail.name: getNextClock
postconditions: Returns a numeric clock value allocated from the transaction's clock sequence.
Advances the transaction clock for subsequent allocations.
invariants: Successive allocated clock values preserve the transaction's ordering.
edgeCases: Repeated calls return successive values from the same transaction-local clock sequence.
stateMutations: The transaction's internal _clock value is advanced.
detail.summary: Allocates and returns the next clock value for the active in-memory storage transaction. Advancing the clock provides monotonically sequenced values for transaction changes.

detail.name: delete
preconditions: The transaction must not be closed.
postconditions: The record identified by id is no longer returned as an active record by the transaction.
invariants: The transaction's closed-state invariant is checked before mutation.
edgeCases: Deleting an id that is not present has no observable record to remove.
Deleting an existing id makes that record unavailable through subsequent transaction reads.
Calling delete after the transaction is closed fails instead of mutating storage.

raises: An assertion failure when the transaction is closed.

stateMutations: The transaction's backing in-memory storage for the supplied record id.
detail.summary: Deletes the record identified by the supplied id within the transaction. The operation is only valid while the transaction remains open.

specTests.when: delete("record-1") is called and the record is subsequently read in the same transaction
specTests.then: The read does not return the deleted record.
The operation raises an assertion failure and does not perform the deletion.

detail.name: entries
postconditions: The returned entries represent the transaction's current visible key-value state.
invariants: Each returned entry associates a storage identifier with its corresponding value.
edgeCases: An empty transaction returns no entries.
Entries reflect transaction-local changes according to the transaction's visibility rules.
detail.summary: Returns the key-value entries currently visible within the in-memory storage transaction.

units.name: keys

detail.name: keys
preconditions: The transaction has not been closed.
postconditions: Returns an array of string identifiers for the transaction's current records.
invariants: Calling the method does not mutate transaction state.
The returned identifiers correspond to the transaction state at the time of the call.
edgeCases: When the transaction contains no records, returns an empty array.
When called after the transaction is closed, the operation fails instead of returning keys.

raises: Error from the transaction closed-state assertion

detail.summary: Returns the identifiers currently represented by the in-memory transaction. The transaction must be open when this method is called.

units.name: values

detail.name: values
postconditions: The returned iterator yields the transaction's stored values from both partitions.
invariants: Iteration does not mutate transaction or storage state.
The iterator yields values rather than storage keys.
edgeCases: When both partitions are empty, the iterator yields no values.
When values exist in either partition, those values are included in the iteration.
detail.summary: Returns an iterator over the values held by the transaction. Iteration includes values from both storage partitions so schema migrations can cover all records.

specTests.then: It yields the values from both partitions and does not yield their keys.
